title: Internal Review, Metrics and Continuous Improvement

content.overview: A professional quality system should examine whether procedures and records are working, not merely whether documents exist. Internal reviews use samples of evidence, trend metrics and follow-up to find recurring weaknesses before they become larger failures.

vocabulary.definition: Structured review of processes and records against defined internal or applicable external criteria.
Documented evidence that a requirement or expected process is not being met.
A measured indicator used to monitor process performance or recurring risk.

sections.title: Audit execution, not document presence
sections.body: A current SOP in a folder is not proof that staff use the right version or complete the required records.

sections.title: Metrics should drive questions
sections.body: Repeated contamination, missed checks, schedule variance or deviations can identify processes that deserve deeper review.

sections.title: Close the loop
sections.body: Findings should connect to correction or CAPA and later verification rather than disappearing after the audit report.

workedExamples: An audit samples actual batch records against the effective SOP instead of simply confirming the SOP exists.
A rising rate of incomplete irrigation records can trigger workflow review before a crop event depends on missing evidence.
commonMistakes: Choosing metrics that no one acts on.
content.practicalApplication: Choose one process, define audit criteria, sample records/execution, document evidence, classify findings and assign follow-up with due dates.
content.summary: Internal review converts procedures and records into a feedback system for repeatability and improvement.
